description: What fabric a garment section will actually accept. The costing optimiser (prism.api.cost_optimiser) reads this to decide how far a fabric suggestion may go. A row is ignored until Reviewed is ticked -- seeded rows are drafts, not rules.

fields.description: Must match a Trim Costing style_name ("T-shirt", "Polo", "Full Zip Hoody"). Callers speaking another dialect are resolved through prism.api.garment_style_map first.
fields.label: Garment Style

fields.description: Canonical section name, or "Any" to cover every section of this style. A section-specific row wins over "Any".
fields.label: Section

fields.description: Until this is ticked the row is ignored entirely and the optimiser falls back to its own conservative defaults. Seeded rows start unticked on purpose: a guessed weight band applied as though it were policy is worse than no rule at all.
fields.label: Reviewed

fields.description: Lightest fabric this section may be cut in. Leave both at 0 to keep the optimiser's relative band (+/-10% of the current weight).
fields.label: Min GSM

fields.description: This section needs elastane. A fabric without it is never suggested, whatever it costs.
fields.label: Requires Stretch

fields.description: Untick for sections that hold the garment's shape -- collars, cuffs, waistbands. They are ribbed for recovery, and no related knit springs back the same way, so their construction is never substituted.
fields.label: Allow Construction Change

fields.description: Leave empty to permit any construction the substitutability graph already rates as a stand-in. Listing families here narrows it further -- nothing outside the list is suggested.
fields.label: Allowed Families

fields.description: Why this rule is what it is. Shown to whoever reviews a suggestion it produced.
fields.label: Notes

name: Garment Fabric Rule
